page: UpCloud HIMEM-2xCPU-16GB is a memory-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 100 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the average tier, while memory write bandwidth for large blocks is poor. Passmark CPU and memory scores, along with Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, reside in the weak category, reflecting the constraints of the shared CPU allocation and limited memory write speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high-density memory profile at a lower entry point, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-throughput multi-core processing. The server is best suited for lightweight databases, caching layers, single-threaded data processing tasks, and basic web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw multi-threaded compute performance.
